chapter: Dallas bands, Ray Charles and family
title: The helicopter wedding and Boston's complaints about pay
summary: Smith played piano himself at a wedding where Boston could not read, and Boston demanded equal pay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: But some of them girls came in there and brought some piano music that we was playing a party downtown there, not too long ago. And they brought one of them numbers that they hear ....(?).... all the time. The man's son got married that night, had a big wedding there, and they had this White girl who wanted to sing this number for this couple. And they was going to catch

a helicopter right after the party and go to Hawaii for the honeymoon. And the helicopter landed right there in the yard -- right there in the yard -- and picked them up. But this girl had to sing this number for them, and as soon as she got through with it, they went and got right on the helicopter and left there.

But I had to play the piano. My brother was (?) right there, sitting right there. We had it out in the yard. So my brother said, "I can't see that." I'm on the stand... See, he was telling the boy that and telling the boss that. "I can't see that." Of course, Snead knew he couldn't read. Because Snead wants to get somebody else if he could, but he can't find nobody else. So I told him, "Well, I'll play." Snead said, "Well, I sure appreciate it." So I got up there and played with this girl singing. That's a number there that ...(?)... girl comes out there and sings. I played it.

Boston can't play it. And he just played by ear. He played it by ear. But he just won't learn it, because he won't study his instrument. Now, he's been playing forty years or better, and he won't study what he's doing! He wants to make a living at it. Be good on what you want to make a living at, if you can! Do the best you can. Jump on in there and be qualified. You can't expect... Now, he's stupid enough, if I pay the boys more money than I do him, he gets mad! Gets mad and then gets stupid enough to want to fight! "I'm your brother. I don't see why you

want to give him more money than me." I say, "Well, learn to read and be qualified. You can't take a shoeshine boy and put him in the judge's seat and expect to give him the same money you're giving the judge. It wouldn't make sense!"
